ABSTRACT
This paper introduces a short-term stochastic Mixed Integer Non-Linear Programming (MINLP) multi-objective
optimization model designed for collaborative planning. It integrates renewable-based distributed generations
(RDGs) like wind and photovoltaic (PV) sources, plug-in electric vehicle parking lots (PEV-PLs), stationary
battery energy storage systems (SBESSs), and mobile battery energy storage systems (MBESSs). The main goal is
to enhance the penetration of green energy and Plug-in Electric Vehicles (PEVs) within the distribution system
(DS). This objective is pursued through the optimization of various planning and operational decision variables,
encompassing the number, location, and size of wind DGs, PV DGs, PEV-PLs, and SBESSs, as well as the number,
sizing, and monthly transportation schedule of MBESSs, along with the hourly scheduling of charging and dis-
charging profiles for PEVs, SBESSs, and MBESSs. The decision variables are concurrently minimized across three
constrained objective functions: total annual expected investment, maintenance and operational costs, power
loss, and voltage fluctuation. To validate the efficacy of the collaborative planning model, a 69-bus DS is selected
as the case study, with five different configurations proposed: Base case, wind/PV/PEV-PL, wind/PV/PEV-PL/
SBESS, wind/PV/PEV-PL/MBESS, and wind/PV/PEV-PL/SBESS/MBESS. The research findings, summarized in
the conclusion sections, highlight the advantages and disadvantages of each proposed configuration regarding
economic, environmental, and technical objectives and their impact on green energy and PEV penetration levels.
1. Introduction
1.1. Motivation
A profound global shift in attention towards environmental preser-
vation has been catalysed by the widespread pollution stemming from
traditional fuel-powered generators. The foremost objective now is to
reduce reliance on fossil fuels and advocate for the widespread imple-
mentation of renewable energy sources (RESs) through distributed
generations (DGs), with particular emphasis on wind and solar photo-
voltaic (PV) systems. Nonetheless, a notable challenge persists in the
erratic and intermittent characteristics of RESs. This inherent unpre-
dictability injects further uncertainty into the system, rendering precise
forecasting challenging and necessitating robust solutions [1 – 3] .
Additionally, the swift proliferation of electric vehicles (EVs) as part
of initiatives to mitigate the detrimental impacts of pollution represents
a significant advancement in the automotive industry. [4 – 6] . Projections
from the International Energy Agency forecast an astonishing 130
million EVs globally by 2030 [7] . Central to this paradigm shift is the
establishment of efficient infrastructure, particularly plug-in electric
vehicle parking lots (PEV-PLs). These facilities, outfitted with robust
communication links, rapid chargers, controllers, and management
systems, are vital hubs facilitating seamless interactions between EV
owners and distribution system (DS) operators. They optimize opera-
tions both economically and technically. Moreover, incentivizing the
adoption of bidirectional EVs with vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capabilities
transforms PEVs into supplementary mobile storage assets within the
system. By harnessing these capabilities, PEVs can effectively mitigate

1.2. Aim
This paper presents a comprehensive strategy for optimizing joint
stochastic planning, focusing on determining the ideal locations and
capacities of various components, including wind DGs, PV DGs, PEV-
PLs, SBESS, and MBESS. Furthermore, it aims to optimize DG opera-
tion, manage the energy expenses and profits of PEV-PLs, schedule the
monthly operations of MBESS, and charge/discharge SBESS/MBESSs.
Moreover, the proposed planning model employs a stochastic approach
to address uncertainties arising from variables such as wind speed, solar
irradiance, load power, energy prices, and the energy and time dynamics
of PEVs. The primary aim is to substantially enhance the integration of
green energy, encompassing RESs and PEVs. Such integrated optimal
planning and operation ensure a reliable power supply to meet the de-
mands of traditional loads, PEVs, and SBESS/MBESS while upholding
system security and accounting for technical constraints.
1.3. Literature review
Numerous research endeavors have been undertaken to tackle the
intricate challenges surrounding the effective integration of EVs into
complex and hybrid power and energy systems. The power and energy
systems literature has outlined several critical components and key-
words pertinent to this integration. These encompass EVs, PEV-PL, Fast
Charging Stations (FCS), V2G technology, Hydrogen Powered EVs
(HPEV), hybrid electric vehicles (HEV), wind DG, PV DG, fixed BESS
(FBESS), MBESS, Hydrogen Energy Storage Systems (HESS), Thermal
ESS (TESS), compressed air ESS (CAES), bidirectional Converters (BDC),
Combined Heat and Power (CHP) units, biomass waste unit (BW), Gas
boilers, Fuel Cells, Diesel distributed generators (DDGs), Energy Hubs
(EHs), Energy Communities (ECs), Integrated Hybrid Power and Heat
Energy Systems (IHES), Aggregators, Virtual Power Plants (VPP),
mechanisms for upward and downward market regulation, reserves,
Energy management system (EMS), Smart Homes (SHs) and buildings,
demand side management (DSM), demand response program (DRP),
network reconfiguration (NR), resilience to contingent events, intelli-
gent programming, Internet of thing (IoT), Uncertainties, Forecasting
methodologies, standalone and grid connected Microgrid (MG), DS,
Transmission Systems (TS), electric, thermal and hydrogen loads, net
energy metering (NEM), independent operators, and electricity markets.
1.3.1. Optimal planning and operation considering MBESS and RESs
In [11], utilizing a MINLP planning model, optimizing wind DGs, PV
DGs, MBESS, and FCSs was conducted to enhance green energy inte-
gration and facilitate smart charger deployment within the DS. In [13], a
joint operation optimization was proposed that combines the newly
introduced MBESS for integration with existing wind DG, PV DG, and
hydropower in the DS. The problem was formulated as a MINLP based
on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) to determine the optimal
charging-discharging profiles of the MBESS. It was proven that the
deployment of MBESS decreases the operational cost of the DS, allevi-
ates congestion, and increases the penetration of RESs. In a separate
study in [14], the authors proposed a stochastic service restoration
model that integrates MBESS fleets, MGs reconfiguration, and RESs.
Additionally, joint probabilistic constraints were utilized to handle RES
uncertainty, where a novel computational method with discrete proba-
bility density function (PDF) scenarios was used for a fast solution. The
effectiveness and scalability of the proposed framework were demon-
strated on IEEE 33-bus and IEEE 123-bus test systems, enhancing the
DS’s resilience against high-impact, low-probability disaster events. A
MILP optimization problem was formulated in [15] to determine the
newly relocated optimal location, the starting time of transportation,
and charging-discharging scheduling for the grid-scale MBESS mounted
on a truck or train. The MBESS surpassed the SBESS in minimizing the
total DS operation and load-shedding costs. However, RESs or EVs were
not considered. Furthermore, in [16], a novel three-level defender-
attacker-defender resiliency-oriented planning and operation model was
proposed for optimizing the sizing and positioning of MBESS in net-
worked MMGs. It utilized an adaptive genetic algorithm for the planning
level and a consensus algorithm for multi-stage decentralized opera-
tional control. This approach determined energy sharing among MMGs,
considering uncertainties through stochastic programming and ac-
counting for external contingencies. MBESS proved more effective for
load restoration than SBESS during extreme events, with capacities
increasing with larger attack budgets.
In [17], a Model Predictive Controller (MPC) was employed as the

1.4. Research gaps and contributions
Drawing upon an exhaustive literature review and harnessing the
authors ’ collective expertise, it becomes apparent that prior research has
only scratched the surface regarding integrating MBESS into the DS.
Some studies have explored the use of PEVs as a MBESS. Additionally,
specific works have suggested hourly relocation of MBESS, a concept
impractical in real-world scenarios. Furthermore, a scant few research
endeavours have explored the combined integration of SBESS and
MBESS to bolster RESs and PEVs integration. Significantly, the study in
[11] represents the sole literature focusing on the practical monthly
relocation of MBESS to augment the penetration level of RESs and FCSs.
However, several shortcomings were identified within this study:
• It is impractical to focus solely on MBESS without integrating SBESS.
Since all MBESS units are relocated at the end of each month, the
absence of SBESS units during the transportation process means
there would be no storage devices available to fulfil their functions in
the interim.
• Emphasis solely on economic objectives while disregarding technical
considerations, which undoubtedly influence optimal cost outcomes.
• Limited analysis restricted to comparing system performance before
and after MBESS allocation, neglecting the necessity to assess various
system configurations.
• The concept of PEV-PL was not incorporated.
This paper addresses these limitations by introducing a compre-
hensive stochastic planning model. This model accounts for economic
and technical objectives and facilitates the seamless integration of RESs
(wind and PV), PEV-PL, SBESS, and MBESS within the DS. The aim is to
bolster the capacity of deployed RESs and PEVs, thereby advancing
decarbonization initiatives within the power and automotive sectors.
The primary contribution of this research can be encapsulated as
follows:
• Constructing a stochastic MINLP optimization cooperative planning
model that includes wind DGs, PV DGs, PEV-PLs, SBESS, and MBESSs
to increase green energy integration in the DS.
• This planning model aims to achieve the optimal location, sizing, and
scheduling of wind DGs, PV DGs, PEV-PLs, SBESSs, and MBESSs by
simultaneously minimizing three objective functions: the annual
total expected planning and operational cost, power loss, and voltage
deviation.
• Developing a flexible and coordinated optimal charging and dis-
charging control strategy for the PEVs, SBESS, and MBESSs.
Furthermore, adopting a monthly transportation schedule for the
MBESSs adds a practical dimension to the research.
• Various configurations were examined and juxtaposed to demon-
strate the efficacy of the proposed planning model under typical
operational modes. The findings from these configurations under-
score the significance of incorporating a hybrid MBESS and SBESS to
maximize green energy integration in both the RESs and trans-
portation sectors.

charging mode is that its departure or current energy level surpasses the
arrival energy level. Conversely, for a PEV to enter discharging mode,

departure energy.

crafted control strategy ensures that each PEV attains its desired energy

lifespan of the PEV ’ s battery and mitigates the need for additional
payments to the PEV owner arising from battery degradation resulting
from frequent usage.

4. Solution method
The ground-breaking Hybrid NSGAII-MOPSO-TOPSIS algorithm, as
elucidated in our seminal contributions [59,60,61,25,22,23,21,29] ,
serves as a cornerstone in addressing the complexities of collaborative
planning models. This algorithm operates with precision, concurrently
minimizing three pivotal objective functions: total annual expected cost,
power loss, and voltage deviation. It plays a crucial role in determining
the optimal number, placement, and sizing of wind DGs, PV DGs, PEV-
PLs, and SBESSs, as well as in configuring the sizes and monthly trans-
portation schedules of MBESSs. Additionally, it orchestrates the intri-
cate, hourly scenario-based scheduling of the charging and discharging
profiles for PEVs, PEV-PLs, SBESSs, and MBESSs with remarkable
finesse.
The hybridization of NSGA-II and MOPSO provides substantial ad-
vantages in solving complex multi-objective optimization problems,
particularly in energy systems planning and operation. This hybrid
approach capitalizes on the complementary strengths of its components:
the robust exploration and diversity-preserving capabilities of NSGA-II
and the rapid convergence of MOPSO. By combining these methodolo-
gies, the algorithm achieves a more effective balance between explora-
tion and exploitation, leading to a comprehensive and well-distributed
Pareto front. In a related previous work, referenced as [60] , the authors
compared the performance of NSGA-II, MOPSO, and a hybrid NSGA-II-
MOPSO approach. The results highlighted the superiority of the
hybrid method in achieving the lowest objective values compared to the
other methods.

6. Conclusions
This paper presents a short-term optimization model integrating
RDGs, such as wind and PV DGs, PEV-PLs, SBESSs, and MBESSs, aiming
to enhance green energy and PEV penetration in the DS. The model
optimizes decision variables, including RDG location and size, and co-
ordinates optimal charging and discharging strategies for SBESS-MBESS-
PEV and monthly relocation schedules for MBESSs. The objective is to
minimize annual costs, power loss, and voltage deviation. Validation is
performed on a 69-bus DS across five different configurations. The
study ’ s findings can be summarized as follows, with the caveat that
these results are specific to a one-year timeframe and may vary for long-
term planning:
• Comparing the configuration of (Wind/PV/PEV-PL) without and with
SBESSs: The incorporation of 5 SBESSs with a combined installed
capacity of 1.17MWh and 0.234MVA led to an increase in the inte-
gration of RESs from 3.1MVA to 3.55MVA and the penetration level
of PEVs from 146 PEVs to 206 PEVs.
• Comparing the configuration of (Wind/PV/PEV-PL) with SBESSs or with
MBESSs: The incorporation of MBESSs alone recorded a combined
installed capacity much lower than the deployment of SBESSs alone,

for EV owners to invest in purchasing new batteries.
7. Restrictions and future work
While previous literature has emphasized the advantages of inte-
grating SBESS and MBESS to enhance system resilience during contin-
gency events, this paper ’ s proposed planning model — encompassing
wind DG, PV DG, PEV_PL, SBESS, and MBESS — was exclusively evalu-
ated under normal operating conditions and for short-term planning
spanning one year. This approach aligns with the core objective of
conducting a comprehensive examination of diverse system configura-
tions (Cases 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5) to elucidate the roles of SBESS and MBESS
in advancing decarbonization efforts within the power and automotive
sectors under standard operational circumstances. Looking ahead,
several considerations emerge:
• The proposed model is verified solely for short-term planning,
covering one year. However, this timeframe may not provide suffi-
cient insight to determine the optimal configuration concerning in-
vestment and operational considerations for long-term planning.
Addressing this limitation represents an area for future research and
enhancement.
• The authors plan to augment the existing planning model to include
scenarios involving high-impact, low-occurrence natural or artificial
disasters. This expansion aims to concurrently enhance both power
industry decarbonization and system resilience.
• Furthermore, the authors intend to conduct a deeper investigation
into the impacts of high penetration levels of PEVs on system
resilience.
